title: Extensions
intro_p: k4o renders Obsidian-flavored Markdown and oliver parses it natively — every extension filter lands as a real document node, not a literal marker. All demos on this page are the pipeline's own output.
hi_p: `highlight` wraps in `<mark>`, `strike` in `<del>` — colored highlights take a color name:
math_p: `math` and `math_block` emit TeX — inline `$…$`, display `$$…$$`. Oliver typesets nothing; the span is yours to hand to MathJax:
math_tr:
$ cat mx.knap {{ f | math }} {{ b | math_block }} $ dogbed render mx.knap -d mx.json

e = mc^2

x = (-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a
callout_p: `callout` turns a value into an Obsidian callout — `> [!type]` under the hood, a `callout-<type>` div on the page. Give each callout its own blank line:
callout_tr:
$ cat co.knap {{ note | callout:"note" }} {{ warn | callout:"warning" }} $ dogbed render co.knap -d co.json

the cap counts the shell too

the href passes through verbatim
task_p: `list:task` and `list:numbered-task` emit checkboxes — the list filter's four modes are `bullet`, `numbered`, `task`, `numbered-task`. Footnotes (`[^n]` + definitions) are on the same flag set:
task_tr:
$ cat tk.knap {{ items | list:task }} $ dogbed render tk.knap -d tk.json
  • done
  • todo
meta_p: The quiet ones: `comment` writes an invisible `%%…%%` note into the source (it never reaches the output — the empty first paragraph below is where it was), `wikilink` emits `[[page]]` (a link by default — a consumer-side resolver can rewrite the target), and `embed` emits `![[x]]` as a placeholder span until a resolver claims it:
esc_p: And the undo button: `escape_md` walks a value back to plain text — inline specials get backslash-escaped before Markdown sees them. For data you don't trust, escape first, format later:
esc_tr:
$ cat esc.knap {{ t | escape_md }} $ echo '{"t":"a *em* and `code` and [x](http://e.com)"}' | dogbed render esc.knap -d -

a *em* and `code` and [x](http://e.com)
